decisions.evidence: Maker R2: “save a link quickly, organise it, search it later, and open the original page” and distinguish things intended to read. Client R2: “Yes, that’s the right direction.”
decisions.note: Conforming high-level direction during goal exploration.

decisions.evidence: Maker R3 presents “single box — just the link, one click.” Client R3: “one link and one click is exactly the speed I want.”
decisions.note: URL-entry save flow conforms during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Maker R3 says the item uses “a title (I generated a readable one from the link)” plus the link and timestamp. Client R3 says it should use the page’s real title and show “description, site icon, and preview image.” Maker R4 presents those fetched details.
decisions.note: The initial card substituted a generated title and omitted required automatically collected metadata; the client supplied the conforming behavior during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Maker R4’s revised saved entry lists “icon + title, a description, a preview thumbnail, and the full address,” but no tags. Client R4 approves: “this revised flow matches what I want.” Tags are only added later by the maker in R12.
decisions.note: The settled early bookmark-card decision still omitted the reference-required per-item tags, and the immediate response did not identify that difference.

decisions.evidence: Maker R3 has the link “drop straight into your list” with no metadata-edit step. Client R3 requires correcting title and description “both while saving and afterward.” Maker R4 adds an editable pre-save review, which the client accepts.
decisions.note: The client corrected an initially immediate, non-editable save flow during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Maker R3 presents a clickable saved link; R4 makes the title open the original page. Client R4 says this “feels natural.”
decisions.note: Original-page navigation conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker R3 places the newest save at the top. Client R3 calls newest-first “a sensible starting order.”
decisions.note: A valid date-added sort is presented and accepted.

decisions.evidence: Maker R3 presents ordinary saving without duplicate handling. Client R3 adds: “if I paste a link I’ve already saved, please take me to the existing entry so I can edit it instead of adding another copy.” Maker R5 then presents that behavior.
decisions.note: The client supplied the missing duplicate-save convergence rule.

decisions.evidence: Maker R4 presents fetched title, description, preview image, and site icon in an editable review and saved card. Client R4 welcomes the review and recognition details.
decisions.note: The revised metadata and editable-review behavior conforms, apart from the separately recorded tag-display omission.

decisions.evidence: Maker R5 limits editing to “title or description.” Client R5 says editing “should let me correct the bookmark’s address too.” Maker R6 adds an Address field and the client approves it.
decisions.note: The client caught the missing URL-edit capability.

decisions.evidence: Maker R5’s edit form contains only title and description. Client R5 says, “Once tags … are part of an entry, I’d expect to edit those there as well.” Maker R12 later presents editable tags, accepted in R12–R13.
decisions.note: The client explicitly supplied the pending tag-edit requirement; its later disposition is linked here rather than counted as unresolved.

decisions.evidence: Maker R5’s edit form contains only title and description. Client R5 says, “Once … notes are part of an entry, I’d expect to edit those there as well.” Maker R14 later presents editable notes, which the client accepts.
decisions.note: The client explicitly supplied the pending note-edit requirement; its later disposition is linked here.

decisions.evidence: Maker R5 says re-saving an existing link gives a notice and “jump[s] to the existing entry and open[s] it for editing.” Client R5: “The duplicate behaviour feels right.”
decisions.note: The central duplicate-save behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker R5 treats path capitalization as equivalent, e.g. `Example.com/Article/` and `example.com/article`. Client R5 explains that differently capitalized paths can denote different pages and “should remain distinct.” Maker R6 implements that distinction.
decisions.note: The client corrected over-broad path matching during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: Maker R5 also treats URLs differing by `www.` or a trailing slash as the same. Client R5 explicitly says, “Ignoring `www.` … and a trailing slash seems sensible,” and R6 retains that normalization.
decisions.note: This broadens the fixed same-URL rule because `www` and trailing-slash variants are not universally the same resource; the client explicitly identified and accepted that departure.

decisions.evidence: Maker R7 searches only “title, description, and address.” Client R7 says “any notes I add … should also be searchable.” Maker R14 later demonstrates note search.
decisions.note: The client supplied the missing full-text note scope.

decisions.evidence: Maker R7 presents the initial search behavior without a case rule. Client R7 states, “Search should ignore capitalisation.” The final scope in R28 explicitly says “case-insensitive search.”
decisions.note: The client added the missing case-insensitive search requirement.

decisions.evidence: Maker R7’s initial search covers ordinary words only. Client R7 requests “`#tag` to search by tag.” Maker R12 later demonstrates tag syntax.
decisions.note: The client supplied the missing tag-query behavior.

decisions.evidence: Maker R7 presents simple live text filtering. Client R7 requests “`AND`, `OR`, `NOT`, and parentheses for combinations,” with quoted operators treated literally. Maker R8 adds the query engine.
decisions.note: The client supplied the missing Boolean and grouping language.

decisions.evidence: Maker R7 presents simple term search. Client R7 requests “quotation marks for an exact phrase.” Maker R8 demonstrates `"roast chicken"`.
decisions.note: The client supplied the missing exact-phrase behavior.

decisions.evidence: Maker R8 presents exact phrases, Boolean combinations, parentheses, NOT, and quoted literal operators. Client R8 says these behaviors match, subject only to the separately recorded operator-case correction.
decisions.note: The query-language structure otherwise conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker R8 decides “Only uppercase `AND`/`OR`/`NOT` act as instructions.” Client R8 says operators “should work regardless of capitalisation” and quoted forms alone should be literal.
decisions.note: The client corrected the operator-recognition rule.

decisions.evidence: Maker R9 models To read and Reference as “Two fixed groups only” and switches an item’s type. Client R9 rejects permanent mutually exclusive types and specifies a To-read status plus “Mark as read,” after which the item remains in the main collection.
decisions.note: The client replaced the divergent type model with the reference unread/read-state model.

decisions.evidence: Maker R9’s proposed organization has only To read and Reference and merely floats “archived/done” as another possible state. Client R9 requires Archive as a separate reversible state, hidden from normal lists/search, available in an Archived view, and distinct from permanent deletion.
decisions.note: The client supplied the missing archive model and its separation from deletion.

decisions.evidence: Maker R10 presents ordinary-by-default bookmarks, Mark to read, a To read view, and Mark as read that removes an item from that view but keeps it under All. Client R10 says the reading behavior “feel[s] right.”
decisions.note: The revised unread/read flow conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker R10 presents Archive hiding items from All and normal search, an Archived view, and Restore. Client R10 approves these behaviors.
decisions.note: Archive and archived-only view conform.

decisions.evidence: Maker R10 says, “I haven’t added a delete action yet” and asks whether Archive is enough. Client R10 requests permanent Delete from normal or archived views, with confirmation distinguishing it from Archive and a safe Cancel.
decisions.note: The client supplied the missing permanent-delete behavior and archive/delete distinction.

decisions.evidence: Maker R11 presents permanent deletion from normal and archived views, explicit archive distinction, and Cancel. Client R11 says the warning and cancellation behavior feel right.
decisions.note: The revised delete flow conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker R12 presents multiple tag chips, editing tags on save or later, clicking a chip to filter, and `#tag` search combinations. Client R12 approves chip entry and click-to-filter.
decisions.note: Tag assignment, filtering, and tag-query syntax conform.

decisions.evidence: Maker R12 claims tags work end to end but presents only free typing and chip creation. Client R12 says, “I do want suggestions from my existing tags as I type.” Maker R13 adds matching existing-tag suggestions.
decisions.note: The client caught the missing tag autocomplete.

decisions.evidence: Maker R13 presents suggestions from existing tags while typing and selection of an exact existing tag. Client R13 says this matches their intent.
decisions.note: The revised autocomplete behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker R14 presents adding/editing notes and searching note content alongside other bookmark fields. Client R14 confirms notes should remain searchable.
decisions.note: Note editing and full-text inclusion conform.

decisions.evidence: Maker R14 presents an ordinary text note displayed on the bookmark. Client R14 adds that notes “support Markdown formatting” and render headings, lists, links, and emphasis. Maker R15 implements it.
decisions.note: The client supplied the missing Markdown-note requirement.

decisions.evidence: Maker R15 presents raw Markdown editing followed by rendered Markdown on save. Client R15 accepts edit-then-see and the formatted display.
decisions.note: The revised Markdown-note behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker R16 presents URL validation and a save-anyway fallback with a manual title when remote metadata cannot load. Client R16 says automatic details “shouldn’t be a requirement” for an unreachable page.
decisions.note: The fallback preserves URL saving while attempting automatic metadata collection.

decisions.evidence: Maker R17 declares the settled “full set” without bulk management. Client R17 adds selection-based tag/read/archive/delete actions and applying an action to every bookmark “in the current search or view—not the entire collection accidentally.”
decisions.note: At the specification gate, the client caught missing selected and current-filter-wide bulk actions.

decisions.evidence: Maker R17’s claimed full scope omits sorting. Client R17 requests sorting “by date added, title, and similar useful choices.”
decisions.note: The client caught the missing sort requirement at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Maker R17’s claimed full scope omits snapshots. Client R17 requests a single local page file for normal pages and preservation of the PDF for PDF links.
decisions.note: The client supplied the missing local snapshot/PDF rule.

decisions.evidence: Maker R17’s claimed full scope omits public archiving. Client R17 says, “I’d also like the option to submit a page to the Internet Archive.”
decisions.note: The client supplied the missing Internet Archive action.

decisions.evidence: Maker R17’s claimed full scope omits reusable filters. Client R17 requests saving “search text plus included and excluded tags” for later reopening.
decisions.note: The client supplied the missing bundle/saved-filter behavior.

decisions.evidence: Maker R17’s claimed full scope omits import. Client R17 requests importing standard browser-bookmarks HTML while retaining titles, tags, and dates.
decisions.note: The client caught the missing Netscape-format import requirement.

decisions.evidence: Maker R17’s claimed full scope omits export. Client R17 requests exporting a standard browser-bookmarks HTML file with relevant metadata.
decisions.note: The client caught the missing Netscape-format export requirement.

decisions.evidence: Maker R17’s claimed full scope omits personal display settings. Client R17 requests default sort, number of displayed items, and text size.
decisions.note: The client caught the missing display-settings requirement.

decisions.evidence: Maker R18 presents sorting by date added and title while retaining sort across filters; R19 adds recently updated. Client R19 says the sort set covers what they would use.
decisions.note: The completed sort decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker R20 presents checkboxes and selected-item actions for add/remove tag, read/unread, archive/restore, and delete. Client R20 agrees actions should target exactly the ticked bookmarks.
decisions.note: Selected-bookmark bulk actions conform.

decisions.evidence: Maker R20 presents “Select all N shown” restricted to the active search/view. Client R20 reiterates that it must remain limited to that filter.
decisions.note: The current-filter-wide bulk-action facility conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker R20 allows selected items to remain targeted even if “filtered out after you ticked them.” Client R20 requires search/view changes to clear selection so hidden items cannot be affected. Maker R21 implements automatic clearing, and the client approves it.
decisions.note: The client corrected a scope leak that could apply actions outside the current filter/view.

decisions.evidence: Maker R22 saves the whole search expression, including included `#tag` and excluded `NOT #tag`, under a name and reopens the dynamic filtered collection. Client R22 says this matches what they wanted.
decisions.note: Saved-filter behavior is functionally equivalent to the reference bundle model.

decisions.evidence: Maker R23 presents one self-contained page snapshot for normal URLs and the original PDF for PDF URLs. Client R23 explicitly approves that model.
decisions.note: Local snapshot and PDF handling conform.

decisions.evidence: Maker R23 presents a separate manual “Submit to Internet Archive” action with a public snapshot link. Client R23 says it should remain separate and manual.
decisions.note: Internet Archive creation conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker R24 presents importing standard bookmarks HTML while retaining titles, tags, and original dates and skipping duplicates. Client R24 approves add-without-replacement behavior.
decisions.note: Netscape-style import conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker R24 presents export to standard browser-bookmarks HTML preserving title, tags, and saved date. Client R24 says export should cover the complete collection and otherwise matches their intent.
decisions.note: Export behavior conforms; the complete-collection clarification does not establish a contrary maker decision.

decisions.evidence: Maker R25 presents persistent app-wide default sort, items shown, and text-size settings. Client R25 approves those personal display preferences.
decisions.note: The required personal display settings conform.

decisions.evidence: Client R25 asks that the item limit be display-only. Maker R26 clarifies that search, counts, and Select all cover the full current result set, including unrevealed rows; client R26 says this resolves the concern.
decisions.note: The linked clarification ends in a conforming display-only pagination decision, so it is not unresolved.

decisions.evidence: Maker R27 says a saved search whose tag has disappeared dynamically returns no matches. Client R27 accepts this and says it should match again if the tag is later reused.
decisions.note: This conforms to a dynamically evaluated saved filter.

decisions.evidence: Maker R27 confirms PDF detection with query parameters and preservation of offline copies when archiving. Client R27 says the remaining edge behavior sounds right.
decisions.note: Snapshot edge behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker R28’s specification gate summarizes fast URL save, editable fetched metadata, duplicate-to-edit behavior, fallback saving, and later editing of all fields. Client R28 says the complete scope matches the agreement.
decisions.note: The settled saving/editing scope conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker R28 summarizes readable bookmark details and live case-insensitive search with exact phrases, Boolean operators, parentheses, and `#tag`, carrying forward the earlier original-link behavior. Client R28 approves the complete scope.
decisions.note: The settled retrieval scope conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker R28 summarizes tags with autocomplete, rendered Markdown notes, To read/read behavior, archive/restore, and distinct permanent deletion. Client R28 approves the complete scope.
decisions.note: The settled organization scope conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker R28 summarizes sorting and bulk tag/read/archive/delete actions with safeguards against hidden or unintended whole-collection items. Client R28 approves.
decisions.note: The settled scale-management scope conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker R28 summarizes snapshots/PDFs, manual Internet Archive submission, uniquely named saved filters, browser-bookmarks import/export, and display preferences. Client R28 approves the full scope.
decisions.note: The settled extended-feature scope conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker R29 reports the real application includes the complete approved scope and 47 passing checks, with network-dependent behavior tested against a local site. Client R29 accepts it as implementing the approved behavior and notes no outstanding failures.
decisions.note: At implementation review, the presented behavior conforms to the reference. The unavailable outbound network is an environment limitation with tested fallback, not a stated functional departure.
